entries.meaning: A person whose job is cutting men's hair and trimming beards. ---
examples: My barber has been cutting my hair for fifteen years.
The barber asked how short I wanted it on the sides.
Both barbers were busy, so I waited by the window.

entries.meaning: A person whose job is washing, cutting, and styling hair. ---
examples: Her hairdresser talked her out of going blonde.
I need to find a new hairdresser since we moved.
The hairdressers at that place are all very young.

entries.meaning: A hairdresser, especially one who cuts and shapes hair in a salon. ---
examples: Ask for Dana — she's the best stylist there.
My stylist is booked through the end of the month.
The salon has six stylists and one receptionist.

entries.meaning: A trained professional who cuts and styles hair. ---
examples: She works as a hairstylist downtown.
A good hairstylist will tell you what won't work.
The movie hired three hairstylists for the cast.

entries.meaning: A shop where people go for haircuts, coloring, and beauty treatments. ---
examples: There's a beauty salon right next to the pharmacy.
She opened her own beauty salon last spring.
Half the beauty salons in town close on Mondays.
entries.contrast: In American English salon is stressed on the second syllable: suh-LAHN.

entries.meaning: A shop where people go to have their fingernails and toenails done. ---
examples: The nail salon on the corner takes walk-ins.
She goes to the nail salon every three weeks.
Two new nail salons opened in that strip mall.

entries.meaning: An older word for a beauty salon. ---
examples: My grandmother went to the beauty parlor every Friday.
The old beauty parlor is a coffee shop now.
In those days every small town had two or three beauty parlors.
entries.contrast: American parlor, British parlour; the word now sounds old-fashioned.

entries.meaning: A person whose job is caring for and painting people's nails. ---
examples: The manicurist filed each nail into a square shape.
She trained as a manicurist after high school.
Two manicurists were working when I walked in.

entries.meaning: A person trained to give beauty treatments to the face, hair, and body. ---
examples: The beautician recommended a lighter foundation.
She worked as a beautician on a cruise ship.
The spa employs four beauticians full time.

entries.meaning: A licensed professional trained in hair, skin, and nail care. ---
examples: You need a state license to work as a cosmetologist.
The cosmetologist looked at my scalp under a lamp.
Most of the cosmetologists here trained at the same school.

entries.meaning: A specialist who treats and cares for the skin of the face and body. ---
examples: The esthetician said my skin was dehydrated, not oily.
She sees an esthetician twice a year.
The clinic has estheticians on staff five days a week.
entries.contrast: Also spelled aesthetician; both spellings are said the same way.

entries.meaning: A hair professional who specializes in dyeing and lightening hair. ---
examples: Her colorist fixed the brassy tone in one visit.
A good colorist costs more than a haircut.
The salon's colorists book up weeks ahead.
entries.contrast: American colorist, British colourist.

entries.meaning: A person who applies makeup professionally, often for weddings, film, or television. ---
examples: The bride hired a makeup artist for the whole party.
He works as a makeup artist on a soap opera.
Two makeup artists were setting up their kits backstage.

entries.meaning: The profession and study of hair, skin, and nail care. ---
examples: She studied cosmetology for a year after graduating.
The community college has a cosmetology program.
Cosmetology licenses have to be renewed every two years.

entries.meaning: The work of cutting and styling people's hair. ---
examples: He gave up teaching for hairdressing.
Hairdressing is harder on your back than people think.
She learned hairdressing from her mother.

entries.meaning: The red-and-white striped cylinder that turns outside a barbershop. ---
examples: You'll see the shop by the barber pole out front.
The old barber pole still turns, but the light is burned out.
Antique barber poles sell for a lot of money.

entries.meaning: The way a person's hair has been arranged. ---
examples: That's quite a hairdo for a Tuesday morning.
She showed the stylist a photo of the hairdo she wanted.
The old photos are full of enormous hairdos.

entries.meaning: Part has 2 distinct senses.
examples: He wears his part on the left.
She switched to a middle part and looked completely different.
Deep side parts were everywhere that year.
She landed the part of Juliet on her first audition.
He has played small parts in a dozen shows.
It is a wonderful part for an older actor.

senses.head: The line on the head where hair is divided and combed in two directions
examples: He wears his part on the left.
She switched to a middle part and looked completely different.
Deep side parts were everywhere that year.

senses.head: A character that an actor plays in a performance
examples: She landed the part of Juliet on her first audition.
He has played small parts in a dozen shows.
It is a wonderful part for an older actor.

entries.contrast: British English calls this a parting.

entries.meaning: A chemical treatment that puts lasting curls or waves into hair. ---
examples: My mom got a perm every fall.
A perm takes about three hours in the chair.
Cheap perms can really damage your hair.

entries.meaning: A short haircut of even length, usually ending around the chin. ---
examples: She cut her hair into a bob over the summer.
A blunt bob works well with straight hair.
Short bobs are back in style again.

entries.meaning: A hairstyle in which the hair is pinned up off the neck. ---
examples: She wore a simple updo to the wedding.
The stylist charged extra for the updo.
Loose updos look nicer in photographs.

entries.meaning: Hair cut short and straight across the forehead. ---
examples: Her fringe had grown into her eyes.
A short fringe suits a round face, she says.
British magazines talk about fringes, not bangs.
entries.contrast: British word; Americans say bangs for hair cut across the forehead.

entries.meaning: One of two bunches of hair tied at the sides of the head. ---
examples: She wore her hair in pigtails until third grade.
One pigtail had already come loose.
He tied her pigtails too tight and she complained all morning.

entries.meaning: A knot or bun of hair worn on top of the head. ---
examples: She twisted her hair into a topknot before the gym.
His topknot came loose halfway through the game.
Half the class showed up in messy topknots.

entries.meaning: A narrow braid made flat against the scalp in a line. ---
examples: Her mother braided her hair in cornrows.
The cornrows took four hours to finish.
He keeps one thick cornrow down the middle.

entries.meaning: A rope-like length of hair formed by matting it together. ---
examples: He's had dreadlocks since college.
One dreadlock had gone gray at the tip.
She tied her dreadlocks back with a scarf.

entries.meaning: A rounded hairstyle of tightly curled hair standing out from the head. ---
examples: He grew out a full afro that year.
She picks her afro out with a wide comb.
The band all wore afros on the album cover.

entries.meaning: A haircut in which the hair on top is cut level and stands straight up. ---
examples: The barber gave him a flattop like his father's.
A flattop has to be cut every two weeks to stay sharp.
Every man in the old squad photo has a flattop.

entries.meaning: A haircut with the sides and back clipped short under longer hair on top. ---
examples: She's growing out her undercut.
The undercut needs a trim every three weeks.
Half the guys on the team have undercuts.

entries.meaning: A haircut in which the hair gets gradually shorter toward the neck and ears. ---
examples: He asked for a low fade on the sides.
That barber does a clean fade.
They charge more for skin fades.

entries.meaning: A very short haircut done all over with clippers. ---
examples: He gave himself a buzz cut in the bathroom.
A buzz cut is easy in the summer.
All the recruits got buzz cuts the first morning.

entries.meaning: A short haircut with the hair standing up on top and cut close at the sides. ---
examples: My father wore a crew cut his whole life.
The barber talked him into a crew cut.
The old yearbook is nothing but crew cuts.

entries.meaning: A short, closely cropped women's haircut with a little length on top. ---
examples: She chopped it all off into a pixie cut.
A pixie cut needs shaping every month.
Two of my friends got pixie cuts that spring.

entries.meaning: Long hair combed sideways across the head to cover a bald area. ---
examples: The wind ruined his comb-over.
He finally gave up the comb-over and shaved it all off.
You can spot comb-overs from across the room.
entries.contrast: The b in comb is silent — KOHM, not "kohmb".

entries.meaning: A hairstyle with the front hair swept up high off the forehead. ---
examples: He keeps his pompadour in place with pomade.
The singer's pompadour was two inches tall.
Fifties pompadours took a lot of work.

entries.meaning: A hairstyle in which the hair is puffed out high and round. ---
examples: Her bouffant barely fit under the hat.
The waitress wore a bouffant like it was still 1962.
Those bouffants were held up with half a can of spray.

entries.meaning: A smooth knot of hair worn low at the back of the head. ---
examples: She wore a neat chignon to the ceremony.
A chignon keeps your hair out of your face all day.
Ballet dancers pin their chignons flat.
entries.contrast: French spelling: said SHEEN-yahn, with no hard ch and no g sound.

entries.meaning: A long curl of hair shaped like a spiral. ---
examples: The baby has soft ringlets at the back of her neck.
One ringlet fell across her forehead.
Damp weather turns her waves into tight ringlets.

entries.meaning: A piece of hair that grows in a different direction and will not lie flat. ---
examples: He has a cowlick right at the crown.
No amount of water will flatten that cowlick.
Both boys have the same cowlicks as their father.

entries.meaning: Hair that stands out in small rough curls instead of lying smooth. ---
examples: Humidity gives me terrible frizz.
A little oil on the ends cuts down the frizz.
The whole point of the treatment is less frizz.

entries.meaning: A knotted, twisted mass of hair that is hard to comb through. ---
examples: She worked a tangle out of the back of my hair.
Wet hair gets tangles faster.
There was one big tangle right behind her ear.

entries.meaning: The end of a hair that has dried out and divided in two. ---
examples: She trimmed off the split ends herself.
Heat styling every day gives you split ends.
You can see a split end if you hold the strand up to the light.

entries.meaning: Small white flakes of dead skin that come off the scalp. ---
examples: He has dandruff on the shoulders of his jacket.
This shampoo is supposed to help with dandruff.
Dry winter air makes my dandruff worse.
entries.contrast: Uncountable in English — never "a dandruff" or "dandruffs".

entries.meaning: The edge along the forehead where a person's hair begins to grow. ---
examples: His hairline has moved back a little every year.
She has a low, straight hairline.
Both brothers have receding hairlines.

entries.meaning: The back of the neck, where the hair ends. ---
examples: The barber cleaned up the hair at the nape of my neck.
She pinned it into a bun at the nape.
He shaved a straight line across the nape.

entries.meaning: The tiny pocket in the skin that a hair grows out of. ---
examples: Each hair grows from its own follicle.
The treatment is supposed to wake up dormant follicles.
Pulling a hair out damages the follicle.

entries.meaning: The tough protein that hair and nails are made of. ---
examples: Hair is mostly keratin.
She had a keratin treatment to smooth her hair.
The bottle claims it puts keratin back into the ends.

entries.meaning: Hair that has lost its color with age. ---
examples: He's got a lot of gray hair for thirty-five.
She stopped covering her gray hair two years ago.
Stress and gray hair seem to go together.
entries.contrast: American gray, British grey — same word, same sound.

entries.meaning: A person with red hair. ---
examples: She's a natural redhead.
The redhead in the front row raised her hand.
Redheads usually have to be careful in the sun.

entries.meaning: The condition of having little or no hair on the head. ---
examples: Baldness runs in his family.
There's no real cure for baldness.
He jokes about his baldness before anyone else can.

entries.meaning: A small area of the head where the hair has fallen out. ---
examples: He didn't notice the bald spot until he saw the photo.
She combs her hair over a small bald spot.
Two bald spots had joined into one.

entries.meaning: The falling out of hair from the head, usually more than is normal. ---
examples: The medication can cause hair loss.
He went to a doctor about his hair loss.
Hair loss after a baby is very common.

entries.meaning: Eyebrows that meet in the middle above the nose. ---
examples: He waxes so he doesn't have a unibrow.
The kid in the drawing had a huge unibrow.
Unibrows are fashionable again in some places.

entries.meaning: Hair that grows on a person's face, such as a beard or mustache. ---
examples: The job doesn't allow any facial hair.
His facial hair comes in patchy.
She waxes the facial hair on her upper lip.

entries.meaning: The soft, fine hair on a young person's face or on the cheeks. ---
examples: At sixteen he still had nothing but peach fuzz.
She shaves the peach fuzz off before applying makeup.
The baby's head was covered in peach fuzz.

entries.meaning: A length of real or artificial hair added to someone's own hair to make it longer or fuller. ---
examples: She got hair extensions for the wedding.
One hair extension had slipped down.
Good hair extensions cost more than the dress.

entries.meaning: A piece of false hair worn to cover part of the head or add fullness. ---
examples: The anchor wears a hairpiece on camera.
You can't tell it's a hairpiece from the front.
Good hairpieces are made from real hair.

entries.meaning: A small wig worn by a man to cover a bald patch. ---
examples: His toupee slid an inch to the left.
Nobody at the office mentioned the toupee.
The store sold wigs and toupees in the back.
entries.contrast: Stress falls on the second syllable in American English: too-PAY.

entries.meaning: An electric device that blows hot air to dry and style hair. ---
examples: The blow dryer tripped the bathroom breaker.
She never travels without a blow dryer.
The hotel had blow dryers mounted on the wall.
entries.contrast: Also called a hair dryer; the two mean exactly the same thing.

entries.meaning: Blowout has 2 distinct senses.
examples: She got a blowout before the interview.
A blowout lasts me about three days.
That place does blowouts for forty dollars.
A blowout at that speed is terrifying.
Old tires cause most blowouts.
The blowout pulled the truck toward the shoulder.

senses.head: A salon service in which the hair is washed and dried smooth with a brush and dryer
examples: She got a blowout before the interview.
A blowout lasts me about three days.
That place does blowouts for forty dollars.

senses.head: A tire bursting suddenly while the car is moving
examples: A blowout at that speed is terrifying.
Old tires cause most blowouts.
The blowout pulled the truck toward the shoulder.

entries.русский: укладка феном; разрыв шины на ходу

entries.meaning: A heated rod used to put curls into hair. ---
examples: She burned her finger on the curling iron.
Leave the curling iron out to cool before you pack it.
The drawer is full of old curling irons.
entries.contrast: Iron is said EYE-urn, not "i-RON".

entries.meaning: A heated tool with two flat plates that presses hair straight. ---
examples: She runs a flat iron over her bangs every morning.
Don't use a flat iron on wet hair.
Cheap flat irons have hot spots that scorch the ends.
entries.contrast: British English calls this pair of tools hair straighteners, always plural.

entries.meaning: A heated tool or product used to make curly hair straight. ---
examples: She left the straightener plugged in all day.
A ceramic straightener is gentler on your hair.
The suitcase had two straighteners in it.
entries.contrast: The gh in straight is silent: STRAY-tuh-nur.

entries.meaning: A small tube that hair is rolled around to make it curl. ---
examples: She slept in curlers the night before.
One curler was still stuck in the back of her hair.
He found curlers all over the bathroom counter.

entries.meaning: A small electric tool for cutting hair or beard to an even length. ---
examples: He tidies up his beard with a trimmer.
The trimmer needs charging again.
The kit came with two trimmers and four guards.

entries.meaning: A small flat metal pin that holds hair in place. ---
examples: There's a bobby pin under the couch cushion.
She held twenty bobby pins in her teeth.
One bobby pin is holding that whole hairstyle together.
entries.contrast: British English calls it a hairgrip or kirby grip.

entries.meaning: A thin U-shaped pin used to hold hair up. ---
examples: She pushed a hairpin into the bun.
The hairpins came out one by one all evening.
He found a hairpin in the car seat.

entries.meaning: A small elastic band used to hold hair back. ---
examples: Do you have an extra hair tie?
She keeps a hair tie on her wrist.
Hair ties disappear faster than socks.

entries.meaning: A small fastener that holds a section of hair in place. ---
examples: She pinned her bangs back with a hair clip.
The hair clip snapped in half.
There were hair clips scattered across the counter.

entries.meaning: A large hinged clip with teeth that grips a twist of hair. ---
examples: She twisted her hair up and grabbed a claw clip.
That claw clip holds thick hair better than a band.
Claw clips came back in style out of nowhere.

entries.meaning: A fine net worn over the hair to keep it in place or out of food. ---
examples: Everyone in the kitchen wears a hairnet.
The hairnet flattened her curls.
The box of hairnets is above the sink.

entries.meaning: One of the short stiff hairs on a brush. ---
examples: The bristles on this brush are too soft.
A boar bristle brush smooths the hair down.
One bristle had bent sideways.
entries.contrast: The t is silent: BRIS-uhl, like whistle.

entries.meaning: A thick clear substance rubbed into hair to hold a style. ---
examples: He put too much gel in his hair.
This gel dries hard and flakes.
The shelf was full of gels and mousses.
entries.countability: countable, and uncountable as a substance

entries.meaning: A light foam worked into hair to give it body and hold. ---
examples: She works mousse through her hair while it's damp.
A little mousse keeps the curls from falling.
The can of mousse was almost empty.
entries.contrast: Sounds exactly like moose, the animal.

entries.meaning: A greasy or waxy product used to slick hair down and make it shine. ---
examples: He combs pomade through his hair every morning.
That pomade smells like an old barbershop.
A tin of pomade lasts about six months.
entries.contrast: False friend: Russian помада is lipstick; English pomade is only for hair.

entries.meaning: A powder or spray that soaks up oil so hair looks clean without washing. ---
examples: Dry shampoo got me through the whole trip.
She keeps dry shampoo in her gym bag.
Too much dry shampoo leaves a white cast.
entries.contrast: Shampoo is stressed on the last syllable: sham-POO.

entries.meaning: A thick conditioning treatment left on the hair for several minutes. ---
examples: She uses a hair mask once a week.
Leave the hair mask on for ten minutes.
The store had hair masks on sale.

entries.meaning: Dye used to change the shade of someone's hair. ---
examples: She buys her hair color at the drugstore.
The hair color washed out in three weeks.
Don't put hair color on freshly washed hair.
entries.contrast: American color, British colour.

entries.meaning: Lighter streaks put into the hair with color or bleach. ---
examples: She got highlights around her face.
The highlights have grown out an inch.
Highlights take twice as long as a single color.
entries.contrast: In the hair sense the word is nearly always plural: highlights.

entries.meaning: Darker streaks put into the hair to add depth. ---
examples: She added lowlights to break up the blonde.
The lowlights made her hair look thicker.
Lowlights are cheaper than a full color.

entries.meaning: A chemical liquid used to bleach hair lighter. ---
examples: She lightened her hair with peroxide in high school.
Too much peroxide will fry your ends.
The whole bathroom smelled like peroxide.

entries.meaning: A chemical treatment that straightens tightly curled hair. ---
examples: She stopped using a relaxer and grew out her natural hair.
A relaxer has to be touched up every few months.
Some relaxers burn the scalp if you leave them on too long.

entries.meaning: The white foam that soap or shampoo makes with water. ---
examples: This shampoo hardly makes any lather.
He rinsed the lather off his face.
Work the lather into your scalp for a minute.
entries.contrast: The th is voiced, as in father: LA-thur.

entries.meaning: Rinse has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Give it one more rinse to get the conditioner out.
She uses a vinegar rinse once a month.
Two rinses and the color still ran.
Give your mouth a rinse after brushing.
One more rinse and the shampoo is out.
Two cold rinses were enough.

senses.head: A quick wash with water, or a light product used after shampooing
examples: Give it one more rinse to get the conditioner out.
She uses a vinegar rinse once a month.
Two rinses and the color still ran.

senses.head: A quick wash in clean water to take soap or dirt off
examples: Give your mouth a rinse after brushing.
One more rinse and the shampoo is out.
Two cold rinses were enough.

entries.meaning: The washing, conditioning, and treatment of hair. ---
examples: The whole aisle is hair care.
Her hair care routine takes twenty minutes.
He spends nothing on hair care.

entries.meaning: An act of cutting the hair off the face or body with a razor. ---
examples: He went in for a haircut and a shave.
That's the closest shave I've had in years.
Two shaves a week is enough for him.

entries.meaning: A foam or cream spread on the skin to make shaving easier. ---
examples: We're out of shaving cream again.
He put shaving cream on and then the phone rang.
A can of shaving cream lasts him two months.

entries.meaning: The thin sharp piece of metal in a razor. ---
examples: The razor blade is dull, so it pulls.
Change the razor blade every week or so.
A pack of razor blades costs more than the razor.

entries.meaning: A razor with one long blade that folds into its handle. ---
examples: The barber finished the neckline with a straight razor.
He learned to shave with a straight razor.
Old straight razors have to be sharpened on a strap.

entries.meaning: An electric device for shaving hair off the face or body. ---
examples: He shaves in the car with a battery shaver.
The shaver died halfway through.
They sell shavers and trimmers in the same aisle.

entries.meaning: Red, irritated skin caused by shaving. ---
examples: He gets razor burn on his neck every time.
A sharp blade and warm water help with razor burn.
Her legs were covered in razor burn.

entries.meaning: A small cut in the skin, especially one made while shaving. ---
examples: He had a nick on his chin from shaving.
One nick and the whole sink turns pink.
There were two nicks along his jaw.

entries.meaning: A small pointed beard on the chin. ---
examples: He grew a goatee over the winter.
The goatee is coming in gray.
Half the band had goatees.
entries.contrast: Stress falls on the second syllable: goh-TEE.

entries.meaning: A complete change of someone's hair, makeup, and clothes. ---
examples: Her sister gave her a makeover before the party.
The show does a makeover in every episode.
Free makeovers at the cosmetics counter bring people in.

entries.meaning: Primer has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A little primer keeps her foundation from sliding.
This primer fills in large pores.
She tried four primers before finding one she liked.
Put primer on before you paint the color.
The stain bled through two coats of primer.
Tinted primers can save you a coat.

senses.head: A cream put on the skin before makeup so it goes on smoothly and lasts
examples: A little primer keeps her foundation from sliding.
This primer fills in large pores.
She tried four primers before finding one she liked.

senses.head: A first coat of paint that seals a surface so the finish coat will stick
examples: Put primer on before you paint the color.
The stain bled through two coats of primer.
Tinted primers can save you a coat.

entries.countability: countable, and uncountable as a substance
entries.contrast: The makeup sense is PRY-mur; the beginner's schoolbook called a primer is PRIM-ur in the US.

entries.meaning: A powder or cream that gives the skin a warm, tanned look. ---
examples: A sweep of bronzer along the cheekbones is enough.
He wore too much bronzer on camera.
The brand makes bronzers in four shades.
entries.countability: countable, and uncountable as a substance

entries.meaning: A shiny, often sticky product worn on the lips. ---
examples: She reapplied her lip gloss in the elevator.
Lip gloss and wind are a bad combination.
There were three lip glosses melting in the car.
entries.countability: countable, and uncountable as a substance

entries.meaning: Lip balm has 2 distinct senses.
examples: I lose a lip balm every week.
He keeps lip balm in his coat pocket all winter.
The drugstore had a whole rack of lip balms.
My lips are chapped; do you have lip balm?
He put on lip balm before going outside.
There are three lip balms rolling around in her bag.

senses.head: A waxy stick or pot used to soften dry lips
examples: I lose a lip balm every week.
He keeps lip balm in his coat pocket all winter.
The drugstore had a whole rack of lip balms.

senses.head: A waxy stick or cream that keeps lips from drying out
examples: My lips are chapped; do you have lip balm?
He put on lip balm before going outside.
There are three lip balms rolling around in her bag.

entries.русский: бальзам для губ, гигиеническая помада; гигиеническая помада, бальзам для губ
entries.contrast: The l in balm is silent: BAHM.

entries.meaning: A pencil used to draw an outline around the lips. ---
examples: She outlines with lip liner first.
The lip liner was two shades too dark.
Her makeup bag had five lip liners in it.

entries.meaning: An eyebrow, especially as something that is shaped and made up. ---
examples: She gets her brows waxed every month.
One brow is higher than the other.
Thick brows came back in fashion.
entries.contrast: Rhymes with cow, not with low.

entries.meaning: A pencil used to darken and shape the eyebrows. ---
examples: She fills in the gaps with an eyebrow pencil.
The eyebrow pencil broke in her purse.
They sell eyebrow pencils in six shades.

entries.meaning: One of the hairs growing along the edge of the eyelid. ---
examples: She has a lash in her eye.
Two coats of mascara and her lashes looked twice as long.
The glue holds the false lashes for about a week.

entries.meaning: A small metal tool that bends the eyelashes upward. ---
examples: She uses an eyelash curler before mascara.
The eyelash curler pinched her eyelid.
Airport security never questions eyelash curlers.

entries.meaning: A mist sprayed over finished makeup to keep it in place. ---
examples: A little setting spray and her makeup lasted all night.
The setting spray smells like alcohol.
She tested three setting sprays on the back of her hand.
entries.countability: countable, and uncountable as a substance

entries.meaning: The use of light and dark makeup to make features look sharper. ---
examples: Contouring takes practice and good light.
She skips the contouring on a work day.
Heavy contouring looks strange in daylight.

entries.meaning: A soft round pad used to put powder on the face. ---
examples: The compact came with a little powder puff.
She patted her nose with the powder puff.
The powder puffs need washing.

entries.meaning: A liquid or cream used to take makeup off the skin. ---
examples: She takes off her mascara with makeup remover.
We're out of makeup remover again.
Makeup remover on a cotton pad works better than soap.

entries.meaning: A small soft ball of cotton used to apply or wipe off liquids. ---
examples: She wiped the polish off with a cotton ball.
There's a jar of cotton balls on the shelf.
One cotton ball soaks up more than you'd think.

entries.meaning: A short stick with cotton on the end, used for cleaning up small areas. ---
examples: She fixed the smudged eyeliner with a cotton swab.
Hand me a cotton swab from the drawer.
The box of cotton swabs is nearly empty.
entries.contrast: British English says cotton bud.

entries.meaning: Colored liquid painted onto the nails and left to dry hard. ---
examples: Her nail polish was chipped on two fingers.
He knocked over a bottle of nail polish.
Nail polish takes forever to dry in cold weather.
entries.contrast: British English says nail varnish.

entries.meaning: A strong-smelling liquid that dissolves nail polish. ---
examples: The whole room smelled of nail polish remover.
We're out of nail polish remover.
Nail polish remover will take the finish off the table.

entries.meaning: The sharp-smelling chemical used to strip nail polish off. ---
examples: Pure acetone dries out your cuticles.
She soaked the tips in acetone to get the gel off.
The salon smells like acetone all day.

entries.meaning: Nail file has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Do you have a nail file? I snagged a nail.
The nail file wore smooth months ago.
She keeps two nail files in her desk.
